extracted.intended_audience: general news readers; people interested in journalism and media ethics
extracted.subtask_description: A news report documenting allegations of plagiarism by a news-site co-founder, the ensuing retractions, internal investigation, editorial responses, and corrective actions; aimed at informing readers about the ethical breach and institutional consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper attribution and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Content must be properly sourced and attributed; Snopes built its brand on properly sourcing information and the retracted articles were described as having 'some or all of its content... taken from other sources without proper attribution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic credibility depends on clear sourcing. Failure to credit original outlets undermines trust and is grounds for retraction and public censure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish verbatim copies of other outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing content 'verbatim' from wire services or other news stories to quickly get a page up (as described in a Slack message) is unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speed-based publishing of another outlet's text — even temporarily — is an anti-pattern. Even if planned edits follow, initial verbatim publication is unethical under widely accepted journalistic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing after publication does not excuse initial plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if he had rewritten the text a few minutes after publication, that would not be considered ethical under widely accepted journalistic standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-publication rewriting cannot retroactively legitimize content that was initially published without attribution. Ethical practice requires attribution at time of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction labeling and public explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Retracted pages were updated to show the word 'retracted' and an explanation that some or all content was taken without proper attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When plagiarism is discovered, sites should mark affected pages clearly, explain why the content was removed or flagged, and be transparent about the nature of the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove monetization from plagiarized content
rubrics_metrics.description: Ads have been removed from the retracted articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing ads prevents continuing to profit from plagiarized material and signals corrective action; it's a recommended immediate step alongside retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal review to determine scope of damage
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial team conducted a review to understand how many articles featured plagiarized content and had found 60 as of the stated time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations should perform a thorough internal audit to identify all affected pieces, document timelines, and determine remedial steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management accountability and disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the co-founder will remain CEO, his ability to publish articles has been revoked; the managing editor was given 'full authority' to address the issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate managerial responses include revoking publication privileges, delegating investigatory and corrective authority to senior editorial staff, and implementing discipline consistent with findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public acknowledgment and apology for violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mikkelson acknowledged 'multiple serious copyright violations' and issued apologies to those whose copyright he violated, to staff, and to readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public admissions of wrongdoing and apologies to affected parties are part of remediation; they should be specific about the nature of violations and steps being taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid obscuring authorship with pseudonyms or false claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The report notes Mikkelson sometimes published under the pseudonym Jeff Zarronandia and that the Snopes bio contained false-sounding claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using pseudonyms or misleading bios to obscure authorship or claim undeserved authority is unethical and compounds the breach of trust when plagiarism occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff-led condemnation and reinforcement of standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple editorial staff members publicly 'strongly condemn[ed] these poor journalistic practices' and emphasized watchdog journalism values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective staff statements and reinforcement of editorial standards help restore internal norms and public confidence; elevating qualified editors to lead remediation supports integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEO/speed tactics do not justify unethical practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Copying text from breaking news to 'scoop up traffic' was described as an SEO/speed strategy used to drive web traffic, which the outlet's staff condemned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traffic-boosting tactics that rely on misattribution or plagiarism are unacceptable; ethical editorial strategy should prioritize accuracy and proper sourcing over short-term SEO gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism includes copying entire paragraphs or nearly whole articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations identified cases where entire paragraphs — and in at least one case, nearly an entire article — appeared to have been copied from other news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism is not limited to short phrases; substantial copying of paragraphs or article structure constitutes serious infringement and warrants retraction and possible legal/copyright consequences.
